title: Working for C. Ferguson's ballroom in Indianapolis
summary: Businessman C. Ferguson hosts the band for three months, feeds them and books most bands passing through.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We finally got to Cincinnati, we sent our business manager over to Indianapolis and he booked the band over to Indianapolis and we worked for a fella named C. Ferguson. This man I'll never forget as long as I live. We arrived in town one evening, afternoon. Mr. Ferguson put us all in the car, took us by the cafe, told the owners of the cafe to give us anything we wanted to eat, all we had to do was sign a check, he'd pay for it.

We stayed and -- in Indianapolis about three months. This man was dear to us, we played for him every week, he had the most popular ballroom in town and he booked most all of the bands that came through town.
What was the name of the ballroom, do you remember?
I can't think of the name of that ballroom either.
I can't think of the name of that ballroom, it was oh -- old building, gutted out, upstairs, it was a small ballroom, but I just can't think of the name

of that ballroom, but it was owned by C. Ferguson, and this man was a very -- quite a successful businessman, because the Internal Revenue was on him at that time. In 1933. So you know when the Internal REvenue was after you in 1933, you must've had some money or you were making money or had made money, you know.
He was in real estate and --
